claims.claim: automatic gearbox and manual gearbox for Toyota Corolla, Carry, Hilux
claims.evidence: Witness photos show a used dismantled engine/gearbox drivetrain assembly with bell-housing areas and wiring/hoses, but no readable make/model, no Toyota identification, and no clear transmission type (automatic vs manual) or vehicle fitment markings.

risks.risk: Cannot confirm the exact vehicle compatibility (Toyota Corolla/Carry/Hilux) or the specific engine/gearbox code; wrong fitment can make the unit unusable.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the gearbox ID plate/label (model/part number) and the engine code plate stamped on the engine block, plus a shot showing any Toyota markings.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic used dismantled engine/gearbox assembly with unknown fitment (worst-case: may not match your car).

risks.risk: Transmission type is unclear (automatic vs manual). Bell-housing areas alone don’t prove which gearbox it is.
risks.proof: A close-up showing the gearbox selector/shift linkage area (manual) or the transmission control/TCU/solenoid pack and connector layout (automatic), or a clear view of the gearbox casing markings indicating type.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as unknown transmission type (worst-case: not the type you need).

risks.risk: Condition/operability is unknown (no evidence it runs, no test results). Heavy grime/rust suggests it may be non-functional or require extensive work.
risks.proof: Video of the unit running (or at minimum a compression test report for engine and a gearbox oil inspection/bench test report), plus any fault-code scan results if available.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not proven working (worst-case: parts-only / needs overhaul).

risks.risk: Missing or damaged components (starter/alternator, sensors, mounts, hoses, ECU/TCU, wiring connectors) could be absent or broken; photos don’t confirm completeness.
risks.proof: A full inventory photo/clip laid out showing all included parts (starter, alternator, sensors, mounts, ECU/TCU if applicable, all hoses/belts, and every connector), and close-ups of mounting points and connector ends.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as incomplete/unknown completeness (worst-case: you must source missing parts).

risks.risk: Internal wear/leaks (seals, bearings, clutch/flywheel condition, gearbox internals) cannot be verified from external grime.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the clutch/flywheel surfaces and any visible seal areas, plus a teardown/inspection report or oil analysis/bench test results.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as worn/possibly leaking (worst-case: overhaul required).

risks.risk: Wiring harness integrity and connector matching are uncertain; hanging colored wires/connectors may be damaged or mismatched.
risks.proof: A clear shot of each connector end (no broken pins), and a continuity/fitment check video or a photo showing the harness fully connected to the ECU/TCU/engine ports.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as wiring/connector condition unknown (worst-case: harness repair needed).

proof_requests: Send clear photos of the gearbox ID plate/label (part number) and engine code stamped on the block.
Confirm whether the gearbox is automatic or manual with a photo of the selector/shift mechanism area or casing markings.
Provide proof it works: video of the engine/gearbox running together, or at least bench test results and gearbox oil condition.
Provide a complete parts list/inventory photo showing what is included (starter, alternator, sensors, mounts, hoses, ECU/TCU if applicable, all connectors).
Send close-ups of mounting points and any visible cracks/repairs on the engine/gearbox casing.
Provide any diagnostic/compression test results and fault codes (if the unit was scanned).
response.reason: The witness can identify the item type as a used dismantled engine/gearbox assembly, so it can be priced at its worst-case as non-proven working and unknown fitment/condition. Seller fitment and transmission-type claims are not supported by readable evidence in the report.
